title: Grateful Dead Live at Haight Street on 1968-03-03
lineage: AUD > Uher RR > DAT > DALCardDeluxe > WAV > CDR

ai_review.summary: Rough mono audience tape captures the historic Haight‑St. flatbed truck gig, but despite lo‑fi sound it delivers a high‑energy set highlighted by a fiery Smokestack Lightning and hypnotic Viola Lee Blues.
ai_review.review: The recording is an old‑school audience capture (Uher reel‑to‑reel with a cheap mic) that is far from hi‑fi – mono, a bit muddy and vocal distortion on Lovelight – yet it remains surprisingly listenable. Musically the band was “on fire,” delivering a scorching Smokestack Lightning, a mesmerizing Viola Lee Blues solo, and strong Pigpen vocals, making this historic free‑street show a real treat for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are enthusiastic (5‑star) and praise the performance despite acknowledging lo‑fi recording; weighting show quality heavily yields a high overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mono Uher reel‑to‑reel tape recorded with a cheap overhead mic; audible hiss, some vocal distortion and occasional pitch wobble, but instruments are relatively clear and the tape is considered listenable for its era.

poor_songs: Lovelight (vocals peter out toward the end)
Viola Lee Blues (messy in places, missing sections)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, impromptu set of classic blues‑rock numbers played from a flatbed truck; transitions are natural and the energy builds through the mid‑set before winding down.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is praised for its hypnotic Viola Lee solo and shredding lead on Smokestack Lightning.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob (Bobby) sings the last verse of Lovelight, providing a memorable vocal moment.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen delivers powerful vocals on Smokestack Lightning and Lovelight; his organ work is noted as strong.
